rules.description: Rule id (`no-empty-catch`, or `plugin/rule`) to a level or a level with options.

accessor-order.description: `get` goes before `set` or `init`, and `add` before `remove`. The fix swaps the two accessors (not offered when a comment stands between or in them).

ambiguous-booleans.description: A plain `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `True`, `TRUE`, `False` or `FALSE` (in the usual casings): a boolean to YAML 1.1 parsers and a string to YAML 1.2 parsers. Lowercase `true` and `false` are fine.

allowed.description: Spellings that are not reported, for example `["on"]`.

check_keys.description: Also check mapping keys. Turn it off to keep GitHub workflow `on:`.

async-suffix.description: An async method returning Task or ValueTask has a name that does not end in `Async`. Overrides, explicit interface implementations and `Main` are left alone (their names are not the method's to choose). Renaming needs the binding layer, so there is no fix.

comment-space.description: A line comment has text right after its marker. Exempt: nothing but whitespace after the marker, a marker repeated (`////`, `##`), `--` separator lines, and a `#!` shebang on the first line. The fix inserts the space.

constant-on-right.description: A comparison with the constant on the left: `null == x` is `x == null`, `1 < x` is `x > 1`. Without the type layer a constant is a literal, `nameof`, `int.MaxValue`-style member or an expression of those; a named constant on the left is not recognised.

debug-assert-message.description: `Debug.Assert` without a message, or with a constant blank one. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Assert` is. No fix.

debug-fail-message.description: `Debug.Fail` with a constant blank message. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Fail` is. No fix.

directive-keyword-space.description: No space between `#` and the directive keyword (`#if`, not `# if`).

doc-comment-space.description: A documentation line (`///`) starts with a single space. More spaces are allowed to indent continuation lines, not on the first line of the comment; a tab or no space is always reported.

document-start.description: The first document does not start with `---`.

file-name-matches-type.description: The file name, up to its first dot and ignoring case, is the name of the first type in the file; a generic type may also be written `Name{T,U}`. Not checked when that type is partial. No fix.

float-style.description: Restricts how plain floats are written. Every option is off until set: `.5` without a leading digit, `1e3` scientific notation, `.nan` and `.inf`. Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. The fix for `.5` is `0.5`.

require_numeral_before_decimal.description: Report `.5`, `-.5e3`: a digit must come before the decimal point.

inheritdoc-on-inheriting-member.description: `<inheritdoc />` without `cref` on a type without a base list, or on a member that neither overrides nor implements anything (a constructor whose signature matches a base constructor is fine). No fix.

key-name-casing.description: A key does not follow one of the allowed naming conventions. The checks are those of eslint-plugin-jsonc: a key with punctuation or whitespace never matches, `camelCase` also rejects `_` and `-`, `snake_case` and `kebab-case` reject capitals. No fix: renaming a key changes the data.

allowed.description: Accepted conventions: `camelCase`, `PascalCase`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case`, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. A key is fine when it matches one.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

max-line-length.description: A line is longer than the configured number of characters.

allow_non_breakable_words.description: Do not report a line that has no space after its indentation (and after a leading `#` run or `- `), such as a long URL.

member-order.description: Members are out of order. Compared with the member before, in the order of the `element_order` option: the kind (fields, constructors, finalizers, delegates, events, enums, interfaces, properties, indexers, operators, methods, structs, classes; in a namespace or file: namespaces, delegates, enums, interfaces, structs, classes), the access (public, internal, protected internal, protected, private protected, private), constants before other fields, static before instance members, readonly fields before the others. A trait only counts between members that agree on the traits listed before it. No fix: moving members would have to take their comments and directives along.

element_order.description: The traits that decide the order, most important first. A trait that is left out is not checked.

no-comment-before-block.description: A comment between the head of an `if`, `else`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `foreach`, `lock`, `try`, `catch`, `finally`, `switch`, `checked` or `unchecked` and its `{`. Put it inside the block or above the statement.

no-default-value-type-constructor.description: `new S()` of a value type with an implicit parameterless constructor and no initializer: write `default(S)` (`Guid.Empty`, `CancellationToken.None`, `IntPtr.Zero`, the enum member with value 0 where they exist). No fix for a target-typed `new()`.

no-duplicate-anchors.description: An anchor name is defined again in the same document; an alias refers to the latest definition above it, which is easy to misread.

no-duplicate-keys.description: An object has the same key twice, after decoding escapes; parsers disagree on which value wins.

no-empty-attribute-parens.description: An attribute with empty parentheses: `[Foo()]` is `[Foo]`.

no-empty-catch.description: A catch block with no statements and no comment swallows the exception silently.

no-empty-comment.description: A comment has no text. A block comment is reported wherever it is; an empty line comment only when it begins or ends a run of comments, because a bare `//` between two comment lines separates paragraphs.

no-empty-delegate-parens.description: An anonymous method with an empty parameter list: `delegate() { }` is `delegate { }`. The fix is unsafe: without a parameter list the method also converts to delegate types that have parameters, which can change which overload is chosen.

no-empty-keys.description: A key is empty or only whitespace (after decoding escapes); some consumers cannot address such a property.

no-empty-statement.description: A lone `;` is a statement that does nothing. A statement labelled `label: ;` is allowed. The fix removes the statement (its whole line when it is alone on it), or turns an empty loop or `if` body into `{ }`; it is not offered for the only statement of a switch section. Overlaps compiler CS0642 for `if (x);`.

no-empty-values.description: A mapping key or sequence entry without a value (an implicit null). Values with an anchor or tag are not empty. Reported at the `:` or `-`.

no-octal-values.description: A plain `0755` (octal to YAML 1.1 parsers, decimal 755 to YAML 1.2) or `0o755` (octal to YAML 1.2, a string to YAML 1.1). Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. No fix: the intended value is not known.

no-region-in-body.description: A `#region` inside a block (a method, accessor or lambda body, or any block in one); regions belong between members. No fix.

no-regions.description: `#region` hides code behind a label. Reported on every `#region` outside a block (a region inside a block is `no-region-in-body`'s), in disabled `#if` branches too; no fix, because removing a pair is a judgment call.

no-undefined-alias.description: An alias names an anchor that is not defined earlier in the same document.

no-unneeded-base-prefix.description: `base.M()` or `base[i]` where the type does not override the member, so `this` binds to the same one. The fix writes `this`.

no-unused-anchors.description: An anchor that no alias refers to. The fix removes the anchor, which changes nothing about the data.

nullable-shorthand.description: `int?` instead of `Nullable<int>` or `System.Nullable<int>`. Name-based: a type of your own called `Nullable` is reported too. Not reported in `using` aliases, `nameof`, `typeof(Nullable<>)` and before a member access (`Nullable<int>.Equals`).

possible-null-dereference.description: A member or element access on an expression the compiler's nullable analysis says may be null. Only code under `#nullable enable` is checked. Off by default: the compiler reports the same thing as CS8602.

qualify-namespace-usings.description: A `using` directive inside a namespace whose name is not written fully qualified (it resolves relative to the enclosing namespace). The fix writes the full name, unless it has type arguments.

quoted-strings.description: Which strings are quoted. Plain scalars that are not strings (`12`, `true`, `null`, dates, ...), block scalars and scalars tagged `!!` are never checked. `required: always` wants quotes on every string, `only_when_needed` reports quotes that change nothing (unless `extra_allowed` matches) and plain strings that `extra_required` matches, `optional` only the latter. Fixes: quoting a plain string and switching the quote type keep the value; removing quotes is unsafe because YAML 1.2 parsers read some strings (`1e3`) as numbers.

allow_quoted_quotes.description: Accept the other quote type when the string contains the wanted quote.

extra_allowed.description: Regular expressions; a string they match may be quoted with `only_when_needed`.

extra_required.description: Regular expressions; a string they match (searched in the value) must be quoted even with `optional` or `only_when_needed`.

quote_type.description: The quotes to use. `consistent`: the first quoted string of the file decides.

required.description: `always`: every string is quoted. `optional`: quotes are free, but must be of `quote_type`. `only_when_needed`: quotes only where the string would otherwise read as something else.

remove-unused-usings.description: A `using` directive that nothing in the file needs (the compiler's hidden CS8019, IDE0005 in the SDK analyzers). Not reported in a file that has compiler errors or `#if` regions, because unresolved or inactive code could be the one using it.

separate-attributes.description: One attribute per attribute list: `[A, B]` becomes `[A]` and `[B]`. Lists on parameters and type parameters are left alone. The fix is not offered when the list has a comment in it.

separate-field-declarations.description: One field or event per declaration: `int a, b;` becomes `int a;` and `int b;`, each with the attributes, modifiers and type of the original. The fix is not offered when the declaration has a comment in it.

single-class-per-file.description: A file holds one class or record: every later one is reported, more parts of the first class (when it is partial) excepted. Structs, interfaces, enums and delegates are not counted. No fix.

single-namespace-per-file.description: A file declares one namespace: every later one, nested ones included, is reported. No fix.

sorted-array-values.description: The elements of an array of only strings or only numbers are not in order (ascending by default; numbers compare as numbers). Arrays of other or mixed elements are skipped. The elements that would have to move (the fewest) are reported and the first report carries the fix; the fix is unsafe because array order can be data.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

min_values.description: Arrays with fewer elements are not checked.

sorted-keys.description: The keys of an object are not in order (alphabetical by default). The keys that would have to move (the fewest) are reported and the first report carries the fix. Comments on lines of their own stay where they are.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

min_keys.description: Mappings with fewer keys are not checked.

order.description: Keys that come first, in this order; the rest follow in the configured order.

suppression-justification.description: `SuppressMessage` needs a `Justification` that says something: not missing, `null`, empty, blank or `"<Pending>"`. Matches the attribute by name. No fix.

tuple-element-names-in-signatures.description: A tuple type in the signature of a method, constructor, property, indexer, conversion operator or delegate whose elements have no names. Overrides and implementations of interface members are left alone (their names are not the member's to choose). No fix.

unreachable-code.description: A statement that can never run. At `fast` depth this is the statement after a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue` or `goto`; with the flow layer it also covers constant conditions and calls that do not return (`does_not_return` in `semantics:`). Only the first statement of a run is reported. Removing it is offered as an editor quick fix only, because unreachable code usually signals a bug. Off by default: the compiler already reports unreachable code (CS0162) and the SDK analyzers add IDE0035.

non_returning_calls.description: Treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`,                       `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. The compiler does not,                       so turn this off to report exactly what it reports (CS0162).

unsafe-numbers.description: A number that a double-precision parser (JavaScript, most JSON libraries) cannot hold: an integer beyond 2^53 - 1, a value that overflows to infinity, underflows to zero or is subnormal.

unused-assignment.description: A value is stored in a local variable and no path reads it before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store). Variables that are captured or whose address is taken are not checked; a variable that is never read at all is reported by `unused-variable` instead. Overlaps the SDK analyzer IDE0059 (unnecessary assignment).

unused-private-member.description: A private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (`analysis: deep`). Members with attributes, overrides, interface implementations, `extern` and `partial` methods are left alone. Overlaps the SDK analyzers IDE0051 (unused private member) and IDE0052 (unread private member).

unused-variable.description: A local variable or catch variable that is never used (the compiler's CS0168), or is only assigned constants and never read (CS0219). Variables captured by lambdas or local functions count as used. Off by default: the compiler already warns (CS0168, CS0219).

use-lambda.description: A lambda instead of an anonymous method. The fix is offered when the anonymous method has a parameter list and no comment before its body; `delegate { }` without one converts to delegate types with any parameters, so it has no fix.

use-literal-suffix.description: A numeric literal cast to `long`, `ulong`, `uint`, `float`, `double` or `decimal` when the literal's own type differs: `(long)1` is `1L`. Not reported for hexadecimal and binary literals cast to a floating-point type, which have no suffix.

use-string-empty.description: `string.Empty` instead of `""` (or `@""`). Not reported where a constant is required: `const`, attribute arguments, default parameter values, `case` labels and patterns.

use-tuple-syntax.description: `ValueTuple<int, int>` and `ValueTuple.Create(a, b)` where tuple syntax `(int, int)` and `(a, b)` is available (not inside an expression tree). The fix is offered for types and `ValueTuple.Create` calls.

using-order.description: `using` directives of a file or namespace are out of order: System first (`system_first`), names in alphabetical order (`compare`), and with the options `static_position` and `alias_position` set to `after`, `using static` directives after the plain ones and aliases after those, each group sorted. `global using` and `using unsafe` stay where they are, and a list restarts at a directive that has a preprocessor directive in front of it (the fix leaves such lists alone). Comments on lines of their own stay where they are; a comment after a directive moves with it. Overlaps the SDK analyzers' `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` .editorconfig key.

alias_position.description: `after`: alias directives come after all other usings, sorted by alias name; `keep`: they stay where they are.

compare.description: `ordinal` compares code points; `culture` ignores case (and puts                           punctuation before digits before letters, a lower-case name before                           an upper-case one that is otherwise equal); `culture_ignore_case`                           leaves names that differ only in case in their order.

static_position.description: `after`: `using static` directives come after the plain usings, sorted (System ones first with `system_first`); `keep`: they stay where they are.

system_first.description: Put `System` and `System.*` before the other namespaces.

description: Configuration of Sudsy, the formatter and linter for C#, JSON and YAML.

analysis.description: Analysis depth for rules: fast (syntax only), standard (within each file), deep (adds project scope).

accessor_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the accessors of a property that is laid out on several lines: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` or the body after `=>` goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

blank_line_after_comment.description: Blank line between the last `//` or `///` comment in front of code and that code: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops it. Comments at the start of a file and `////` comments keep theirs.

blank_line_before_comment.description: Blank line between a statement, member or switch section and a `//` comment on the lines before the next one (not `////`): `preserve` keeps the source's; `require` adds one.

blank_lines_after_block.description: Blank line after a statement, member or switch section that ends with a closing brace: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `require` adds one before the next statement, member or section.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it; `always` requires one between any two members of a type or namespace and between the `using` directives and what follows them, except between two fields or two `using` directives (enum members as `separate`).

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

brace_same_line.description: Elements whose opening brace stays on the line of the declaration or statement although `brace_newline` is `all`: `types`, `methods`, `properties`, `accessors`, `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `control_blocks`, `lambdas`, `object_collection_array_initializers` (types include namespaces, methods include constructors, operators and local functions, properties include indexers and events, control blocks include `switch` statements and bare blocks).

catch_line.description: `catch` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

closing_paren_line.description: The `)` of a parameter, argument or attribute argument list that does not fit on one line: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own after the last item; `same_line` right after the last item.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

derive_symbol_sets.description: Also parse with sets of symbols taken from the `#if` and `#elif` conditions of the file (the empty set, all symbols, then each symbol, then pairs and so on, at most 16 sets, after those of `preprocessor_symbol_sets`) until every branch has been active once, and format the branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` from those parses. A branch no set activates stays as it is.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

else_line.description: `else` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when a call other than the last has an argument with a block body (a lambda), even if the chain would fit.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain a property access stays on the line of the call after it (`.A.B()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own.

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. The file is also parsed with each set (a set replaces `preprocessor_symbols`), and the `#if` branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` but active under a set are formatted from that parse. Empty (the default) leaves inactive branches as they are.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no              comment and no `switch` or label in it. Types, namespaces and `switch` bodies are              not affected.

preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with              `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position:              after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the              groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with              it. Lists with preprocessor directives are left alone.

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

exclude.description: Globs of files to leave alone, in addition to ignore files.

extends.description: Presets (`preset:<language>/<name>`) or config files, applied in order.

array_bracket_spacing.description: Spaces inside the brackets of a one-line sequence or array: `[ 1, 2 ]` or `[1, 2]`.

bracket_spacing.description: Spaces inside the braces of a one-line mapping or object: `{ a: 1 }` or `{a: 1}`.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

include.description: Globs of the files to format and lint (everything when empty).

array_bracket_spacing.description: Spaces inside the brackets of a one-line sequence or array: `[ 1, 2 ]` or `[1, 2]`.

bracket_spacing.description: Spaces inside the braces of a one-line mapping or object: `{ a: 1 }` or `{a: 1}`.

collapse.description: Objects and arrays on one line: `preserve` keeps one that has a line break between its brackets expanded and puts the others on one line if they fit; `always` puts every one that fits on one line; `never` puts every non-empty one on several lines; `opening_break` keeps an object expanded when a line break follows its opening brace and puts every array that fits on one line.

dialect.description: JSON or JSONC (comments, trailing commas); `auto` decides by file name.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

trailing_commas.description: Trailing commas after the last item of a multi-line object or array (JSONC only).

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

accessor_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the accessors of a property that is laid out on several lines: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` or the body after `=>` goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

blank_line_after_comment.description: Blank line between the last `//` or `///` comment in front of code and that code: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops it. Comments at the start of a file and `////` comments keep theirs.

blank_line_before_comment.description: Blank line between a statement, member or switch section and a `//` comment on the lines before the next one (not `////`): `preserve` keeps the source's; `require` adds one.

blank_lines_after_block.description: Blank line after a statement, member or switch section that ends with a closing brace: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `require` adds one before the next statement, member or section.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it; `always` requires one between any two members of a type or namespace and between the `using` directives and what follows them, except between two fields or two `using` directives (enum members as `separate`).

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

brace_same_line.description: Elements whose opening brace stays on the line of the declaration or statement although `brace_newline` is `all`: `types`, `methods`, `properties`, `accessors`, `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `control_blocks`, `lambdas`, `object_collection_array_initializers` (types include namespaces, methods include constructors, operators and local functions, properties include indexers and events, control blocks include `switch` statements and bare blocks).

catch_line.description: `catch` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

closing_paren_line.description: The `)` of a parameter, argument or attribute argument list that does not fit on one line: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own after the last item; `same_line` right after the last item.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

derive_symbol_sets.description: Also parse with sets of symbols taken from the `#if` and `#elif` conditions of the file (the empty set, all symbols, then each symbol, then pairs and so on, at most 16 sets, after those of `preprocessor_symbol_sets`) until every branch has been active once, and format the branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` from those parses. A branch no set activates stays as it is.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

else_line.description: `else` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when a call other than the last has an argument with a block body (a lambda), even if the chain would fit.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain a property access stays on the line of the call after it (`.A.B()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own.

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. The file is also parsed with each set (a set replaces `preprocessor_symbols`), and the `#if` branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` but active under a set are formatted from that parse. Empty (the default) leaves inactive branches as they are.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no              comment and no `switch` or label in it. Types, namespaces and `switch` bodies are              not affected.

preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with              `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position:              after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the              groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with              it. Lists with preprocessor directives are left alone.

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

files.description: Globs relative to the config file; the override applies to files that match any.

bracket_spacing.description: Spaces inside the braces of a one-line mapping or object: `{ a: 1 }` or `{a: 1}`.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.
